say: Some songs sound happy and sad at the same time.
And it all comes from one borrowed note.
show: Happy and sad at once? It comes from *one borrowed note*.

say: Here is a happy progression in C major.
show: A happy progression in C major: *C, F, C*.

say: Now lower the A by one key.
It does not belong to C major.
It is borrowed, from C minor.
show: That's *F minor*, borrowed from C minor.

say: F minor sounds like a sigh.
Right before home, it makes the ending ache.
show: F major sounds open. F minor sounds like a *sigh*.

say: A flat leans down to G,
one key, straight into the C chord.
show: *A♭ falls to G*, one key down into the C chord.
On guitar: F, then move *one finger*: F minor.

say: Once you know it, you will hear this chord in ballads everywhere.
show: Now you'll hear this chord in *ballads everywhere*.

say: That was one Fret key lesson.
There are more than three hundred, each about five minutes.
show: One *Fretkey* lesson. More than 300, each about five minutes.
